root.name: Nimzo-Indian Defense: Dilworth Gambit
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. e4

overview: White plays 4.e4 against the Nimzo-Indian, offering the pawn: Black takes with 4...Nxe4 and White tries 5.Qg4 or Qf3 to hit g7 and b4, aiming for a wild attack. Black replies ...Nxc3 and ...Bxc3+ and consolidates. The line is a rare surprise gambit.

white_ideas.idea: Sacrifice the e4 pawn for development and an attack with Qg4 or Qf3

black_ideas.idea: Take on e4 and trade the knights to simplify
Return the pawn if needed to consolidate

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with Black pieces active
White tries to exploit Black's uncastled king

gambit.notes: Black can take on e4 and keep the pawn.

level.notes: Dubious so not a good repertoire choice.

gambit.reason: 4.e4 offers a pawn that Black can keep.

structure.reason: Central pawn exchanges open the position.

plans.reason: White plays for quick development against the uncastled Black king.
